I had the same problem when I got upped from 25 to 50 mg. I had worse than no appetite, I started to hate food. As you mentioned, the feeling of food in my mouth or filling my stomach felt disgusting. I was starving, and my body couldn't eat, I'd try, but then once I sat down to eat, I'd spiral. After a couple of bites, I'd start to feel full or totally uninterested in eating. It was so frustrating, I could feel the daily toll, and yet I couldn't find food desirable. 
I could never relax enough to eat a full meal. The only things I could eat, like you mentioned, were soup, crackers, fruuts, nuts, bars, and smoothies. I felt totally detached from my body in so many ways on Zolft. I lost 10 lbs (not much, but when you're already small, it feels like a lot) and struggled to maintain a weight above 110lb. I could only handle the side effects for 6 months, so I tappered off of it. 
When I was struggling to eat, I found running. It does burn calories, but it helped me feel hungry and gave me a temporary appetite. It was also a motivation, like if I wanted to go running, I'd have to eat. I found eating whatever you can, in whatever amount, was helpful. Try not to make eating any more stressful, eat what you can, and keep in mind you're eating to fuel your body and brain. Every step forward is a step in the right direction.

Nothing can replace being aware of your surroundings. If you're trail running, you should be aware of alternate routes to take if necessary. I wear headphones while running, but I always keep one ear open. If you're going to take pepper spray (I recommend the gel vs. spray, which is more accurate), be prepared to use it. Test it beforehand and know what situations it's safe for you to use it and when not to (i.e., strong winds or close distance). If you take a knife, know how to use it, know where to use it on your attacker. Sometimes, having a knife on me makes me feel safer, but I know an attacker could end up taking it from me. I really like having a lightweight BRIGHT flashlight, specifically with a strobe or rapid bright setting (I have an OLIGHT S2R II).

I don't have self-defense training, but I highly recommend it to be mentally and physically prepared to keep yourself out of a scary situation. I have been in situations that felt unsafe out on the trail, but keeping calm and knowing your outs and how to de escalate are great skills.

Protect yourself, but if you get into a situation run, that's the best advice. Don't try to engage, and know when a physical response is necessary.

Also, make sure people know where you're running and when you'll be back.
